narrative.overview: The Studio behaves like a living operations book laid open beside Dillon: exact, scannable, dense when the work demands it, and quiet enough that state and decisions remain obvious. Its visual language joins an editorial ledger's rules and notation with a modern control room's status vocabulary.
keyCharacteristics: Square ledger geometry and explicit dividers
Navy command surfaces paired with warm working paper
Orange reserved for owner action and current focus
Mono notation for state, evidence, counts, and versions
Responsive structure that turns into a mobile operating console

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Orange belongs to owner action, active focus, or meaningful attention. It must not become ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Data Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Mono appears only when the text behaves like state, a version, a count, a date, or an identifier.

rules.name: The Flat Record Rule
rules.body: Ordinary rows and records never receive floating-card shadows.

dos: Do keep client identity visible beside every recommendation, queue item, request, and result.
Do use density where Dillon is comparing work and quiet space where he is making a decision.
Do make status, stale state, and approval gates explicit in words as well as color.
Do preserve one component vocabulary across desktop and mobile.
donts: Don't replace operational structure with generic analytics cards.
Don't use gradients, glow, glass, or decorative motion as substitutes for information.
Don't scatter orange across inactive regions.
Don't hide consequential actions behind ambiguous icon-only controls.
Don't make mobile a read-only afterthought.
